SPACE MISSION DESIGN SIM
An INCREDIBLES Production | NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

SPACE MISSION DESIGN SIM is an interactive, 2D space exploration and mission design simulator that allows players to experience the challenges of planning, designing, and executing space missions.

Inspired by real-world space exploration and NASA resources, the game enables players to construct rockets part by part, design spacecraft, deploy satellites, build planetary rovers, and explore space through interactive missions.

Players must make important engineering decisions involving fuel, thrust, spacecraft mass, power, budget, orbital trajectories, and communication systems. Every decision affects mission performance, creating realistic possibilities of mission success or failure.

The game features multiple mission objectives, different difficulty levels, resource management, interactive simulations, and post-mission analysis. It also encourages teamwork through collaborative mission-planning roles.

By combining space science, engineering concepts, and interactive gaming, SPACE MISSION DESIGN SIM aims to make space exploration accessible, educational, and engaging for everyone.

Team: INCREDIBLES

Team Leader: Abhinav R Kurup

Lead Developers: Abhinav R Kurup, Sooraj DS, Gopika, Krishnaveni, Athira Raj

Event: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
details:
SPACE MISSION DESIGN SIM

An INCREDIBLES Production

1. Project Overview

SPACE MISSION DESIGN SIM is an interactive 2D space mission design and simulation game that introduces players to the science and engineering behind space exploration. Players can design rockets, assemble spacecraft, deploy satellites, build planetary rovers, and execute missions through an engaging simulation environment.

2. Problem Statement

Space science and mission engineering can be difficult for beginners to understand because they involve complex scientific concepts, calculations, and engineering decisions. Traditional learning methods often lack practical interaction and experimentation.

Our project addresses this challenge by transforming space mission planning into an interactive gaming experience where players can experiment, make decisions, face realistic challenges, and learn through simulation.

3. Proposed Solution

We propose a browser-based 2D space mission simulator that allows users to experience the complete mission development process, from selecting an objective to launching a rocket and evaluating mission results.

Players can:

  • Assemble rockets using individual components.
  • Design spacecraft, satellites, and planetary rovers.
  • Select mission objectives and destinations.
  • Manage fuel, mass, power, budget, and communication.
  • Control rocket launches and stage separation.
  • Simulate orbital insertion and payload deployment.
  • Experience mission failures based on engineering decisions.
  • Analyse mission performance through detailed reports.

4. Key Features

  • Rocket Builder: Modular rocket construction with engines, fuel tanks, boosters, and separation systems.
  • Spacecraft Designer: Build satellites, landers, and scientific payloads.
  • Mission Selection: Multiple objectives, including Earth observation, Moon landing, Mars exploration, and satellite deployment.
  • Physics Simulation: Gravity, thrust, fuel consumption, atmospheric drag, and orbital motion.
  • Resource Management: Live monitoring of mass, fuel, power, budget, and communications.
  • Mission Failure System: Engineering-related failures and unexpected challenges.
  • Mission Evaluation: Scoring based on success, scientific value, and resource efficiency.
  • Learning Mode: Simple explanations of aerospace and orbital mechanics.
  • Sandbox Mode: Experiment freely without strict mission restrictions.
  • Team Mode: Collaborative mission planning with up to four participants.

5. NASA Data Integration

The project uses NASA's publicly available scientific resources and datasets to support educational accuracy.

Potential sources include:

  • NASA Open APIs
  • NASA Planetary Data System
  • NASA Solar System Exploration
  • NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive

NASA-sourced information supports planetary descriptions, scientific facts, imagery, and educational content.

6. Educational Impact

The game helps players understand:

  • Rocket propulsion and staging.
  • Spacecraft components and engineering.
  • Orbital mechanics and satellite deployment.
  • Fuel and power management.
  • Planetary exploration.
  • Scientific instruments and data collection.
  • Mission planning and problem-solving.

It encourages experimentation, critical thinking, teamwork, and STEM learning.

7. Target Audience

  • Students and beginners interested in space science.
  • STEM educators and institutions.
  • Space exploration enthusiasts.
  • Participants in science and engineering competitions.

8. Expected Outcome

SPACE MISSION DESIGN SIM aims to provide an accessible and engaging platform for learning about space mission engineering. By combining interactive gameplay with NASA-based scientific resources, it makes complex aerospace concepts easier to understand through practical experimentation.

9. Technology Stack

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript / React.
  • Game Engine: HTML5 Canvas / Phaser.
  • Physics: Custom 2D physics and orbital calculations.
  • Data Sources: NASA Open APIs and official NASA datasets.
  • Storage: LocalStorage / IndexedDB.
  • Deployment: GitHub Pages or another static web hosting platform.
